ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, with the center being a six-membered carbon/nitrogen skeleton containing N, and there are several curved arrows inside the ring; the problem requires ignoring the arrows. The upper left and upper right of the central skeleton are each directly connected to an Ar, and the right side is also connected to another Ar through a downward CH2 chain; the N at the bottom is connected downward to a Bn. Hydrogens are not drawn in the figure, and according to the problem, bonds involving hydrogen are not counted. Counting reasoning: According to the specified method, first count the non-hydrogen bonds outside the interior of the unexpanded aryl groups: there are 5 bonds in the central open N/C skeleton; the two direct core–Ar connecting bonds are 2; the right-side core–CH2–Ar chain has 2 bonds; the N–Bn connecting bond is 1. Therefore the externally visible non-hydrogen bonds total 5 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 10. Then expand the abbreviated groups: the three Ar groups each contribute 6 ring bonds of one aromatic ring, for a total of 3 × 6 = 18; the Bn group contributes 6 ring bonds of a benzene ring and 1 bond between the benzylic carbon and the benzene ring, for a total of 7. The total is 10 + 18 + 7 = 35.

method.method_draft: First count the non-H bonds visible outside the expanded aromatic interiors: five bonds in the open central N/C framework, two direct core–Ar attachment bonds, two bonds in the right-side core–CH2–Ar chain, and one N–Bn attachment bond, giving 10. Then expand the labels: the three Ar groups contribute 3 × 6 = 18 aromatic ring bonds; the Bn group contributes 6 phenyl-ring bonds plus 1 benzylic C–phenyl bond = 7. Add these: 10 + 18 + 7 = 35.
